claim: Human and DocAble comparison: per-document median checker reductions; increased-finding counts; semantic 20 better, 41 parity, 1 worse of 62; document-criterion gains and regressions. Undefined XLSX percentage preserved; parity is not accessibility equivalence.
alt: Human and DocAble comparison: per-document median checker reductions; increased-finding counts; semantic 20 better, 41 parity, 1 worse of 62; document-criterion gains and regressions. Undefined XLSX percentage preserved; parity is not accessibility equivalence.
caption: *Remediation compared with the human reference.* (a) Median reduction in checker findings from the original; (b) frequency of increased findings; (c) semantic comparison of DocAble and human outputs under the project rubric; (d) criterion-level gains and regressions relative to the original. DocAble led on PDF and DOCX checker reductions and image-description gains; the human workflow led on PPTX checker reductions. Parity denotes similar measured improvement, not equivalent accessibility. [short: Human-reference remediation results]
bw_encoding: Human: outlined white bars with black diagonal hatching. DocAble: dark solid bars. H/D direct labels identify every paired result independently of fill, including zeros. Panel (d) uses position relative to a strong zero line and signed counts for gains/losses; the semantic comparison panel retains category labels and exact counts.

layout_review.reason: Improve the four-panel comparison at printed size without changing the data or estimands. Increase paired-bar thickness and border weight; give Human bars black hatching and DocAble bars dark solid fill. Prefix every comparison value with H or D so zero-length bars remain attributable. Panel (d) has a strong zero divider, signed gain labels and nonzero loss counts, with explicit Losses ← 0 → Gains directions. Preserve undefined XLSX reduction, unequal checker denominators, semantic counts 20/41/1, the ±1 parity band, and document–criterion rather than unique-defect counts. Retain all four panels and original/native comparison versions.

validation_history.visual_review: Standalone native proof inspected: readable text, no clipping or overlap; patterns and line styles distinguish series. Counts, no-record shading, and cohort distinctions retained. Full pool gate remains parent integration check.
